events.title: The Beatles' First Appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show
events.description: The Beatles performed on The Ed Sullivan Show in the United States, drawing an estimated 73 million viewers, one of the largest television audiences in American history at the time.
events.significance: This broadcast marked the start of the British Invasion in American popular music and cemented the Beatles' global stardom, reshaping popular music and youth culture.

events.title: Apollo 14 Returns to Earth
events.description: Apollo 14 splashed down in the Pacific Ocean after the third crewed lunar landing mission, with astronauts Alan Shepard, Edgar Mitchell, and Stuart Roosa safely returning. Shepard and Mitchell had explored the Fra Mauro highlands on the Moon.
events.significance: The mission restored confidence in the Apollo program after the Apollo 13 emergency and returned valuable lunar samples for scientific study.

events.title: John Quincy Adams Elected President by the House of Representatives
events.description: After no candidate won a majority of electoral votes in the 1824 election, the U.S. House of Representatives chose John Quincy Adams as president over Andrew Jackson on the first ballot.
events.significance: The outcome, labeled the 'corrupt bargain' by Jackson's supporters, fueled political realignment and led to the formation of the Democratic Party and Jackson's victory in 1828.

events.title: Guadalcanal Campaign Ends
events.description: Japanese forces completed their evacuation of Guadalcanal, and the Allies secured the island, ending the six-month campaign in the Solomon Islands.
events.significance: The Allied victory was a major turning point in the Pacific War, shifting the strategic initiative away from Japan and opening the path for advances toward Japan.
